There's xor for Bool , Xor is not taken for the Prop version. Why is it named Xor'?

I guess its difficult to make the case to change this given the gains from that wouldbe non existant.

Also , I was a bit confused when discovering the Op variant. For example OrOp , why doesn't Prop just implement OrOp instead of having Or as its own inductive type?
I guess the second question applies to XorOp , AndOp etc...
The purpose of OrOp smells computational , while Or is constructive.

Oh, XorOp was previously called Xor so Xor' wasn't available; seems like nobody cared to fix Xor' after the change. For your second question, OrOp / AndOp / XorOp are for the bitwise ||| / &&& / ^^^ operations. Prop doesn't have bits so it doesn't make sense there.
docs#Xor' is a very silly predicate in my personal view, considering that it's equivalent to \neg x \iff y. I'd imagine that the fact no one has fixed it reflects the lack of usage.

Violeta Hernández said:

docs#Xor' is a very silly predicate in my personal view, considering that it's equivalent to \neg x \iff y. I'd imagine that the fact no one has fixed it reflects the lack of usage.

Well doing a 

grep --color=auto -r --include="*.lean" "Xor'" . | wc -l

in mathlib gives 50 matches. Replacing Xor' with Xor is doable. And also reflects lack of usage as you said.

look what i found in Logic/Basic.lean

/--
2025-07-31. Upstream `Xor` has been renamed to `XorOp`.
2025-09-16. The deprecation for `Xor` has been removed.
Anytime after v4.25.0-rc1 lands we rename this back to `Xor`.
-/
/-- `Xor' a b` is the exclusive-or of propositions. -/
def Xor' (a b : Prop) := (a ∧ ¬b) ∨ (b ∧ ¬a)
